title: Why You Make Different Choices When Options Are Framed Differently
hook: Ever choose differently when the same option is just worded differently?

narration.text: Your choices are often swayed by how information is presented to you.
This is known as the framing effect, a cognitive bias.
People prefer avoiding losses over acquiring equivalent gains.
So, a '90% fat-free' label sounds better than '10% fat'.
The underlying information is identical, but the frame changes perception.
Understanding this helps us make more conscious decisions.
It also reveals how others might influence our thinking.
Have you noticed how wording impacts your choices in daily life?

description: Discover the framing effect, a fascinating cognitive bias that explains why we often make different choices based on how information is presented. Learn how subtle changes in wording can influence our decisions, even when the underlying facts remain the same.
topic: Why you often make different choices when options are framed differently, explaining the framing effect.
